weeks.title: Java foundation and a small tested model

tasks.title: tool and Git check
tasks.description: Check java --version, javac --version, mvn --version, git --version; open the intended work folder in VS Code and confirm Java support. Decide where future exercise/app code will live.
tasks.criteria: versions and paths recorded in PROGRESS; compile/run a tiny class from the terminal, or record the exact blocker and next fix. Do not install every later tool today.

tasks.title: Java diagnostic
tasks.description: Spend at most 15m reviewing a current example, then independently trace constructor/static/instance execution and write a small object-based exercise. Use your current Client or sports-store work as context.
tasks.criteria: one runnable attempt and five answered questions: class vs object, when a constructor runs, object field vs local variable, static vs instance, and method argument vs return value. Record uncertain answers for repair.

tasks.title: define the project slice
tasks.description: Write a short domain note for StudyTask: title, status, optional due date, and identifier; define create/find/change-status behavior.
tasks.criteria: three operations and four acceptance cases written in your own words, including blank title and missing ID. No framework or database yet.

tasks.title: inspect current AGH briefs
tasks.description: Check the four subjects' actual current exercises and deadlines.
tasks.criteria: all four rows in the deadline board have a source and next action; unresolved dates are explicitly unknown with a follow-up action.

tasks.title: OS baseline
tasks.description: Review one current Bash exercise. In a disposable directory, independently demonstrate quoting a filename with spaces, one pipeline, and permission inspection.
tasks.criteria: three command/output examples plus one explanation of quoting. Avoid practicing destructive commands on real coursework.

tasks.title: targeted OOP reading
tasks.description: Read only the constructor/encapsulation material exposed by Day 1.
tasks.criteria: explain constructor vs normal method and private state in three sentences without notes.

tasks.title: implement the domain exercise yourself
tasks.description: Create a StudyTask class and status enum; use a constructor and methods to express the chosen rules. Keep input/output separate from the model.
tasks.criteria: a small runner creates two independent tasks, changes one status, and shows that the other object's state is unchanged; sources compile. Record one design question instead of adding a framework.

tasks.title: IBM starting point
tasks.description: Open your actual enrolled certificate progress and complete one suitably small segment/lab, or continue the current lab.
tasks.criteria: course/unit name, completed assessment or executable artifact, and one next step logged. If new, create/run a notebook with three Python expressions/functions and explain the outputs.

tasks.title: collections/interface lookup
tasks.description: Review typed lists/maps and a small Java interface.
tasks.criteria: explain why a lookup operation may be absent and which collection you will use.

tasks.title: in-memory storage
tasks.description: Define a small repository interface and an in-memory implementation; create/list/find tasks through it. Keep it single-threaded and simple.
tasks.criteria: store three tasks, retrieve an existing ID, handle a missing ID deliberately, and explain the interface's role. Show the operations in a runnable exercise. Full generic abstractions are unnecessary.

tasks.title: current Java lab
tasks.description: Check the actual rubric. If the October 20 sports-store task remains relevant, independently verify Scanner input and discount boundaries; otherwise work on the latest task.
tasks.criteria: compile/run evidence, at least three rubric-derived checks, and a precise remaining-work list. Preserve its required console behavior and submission file rules.

tasks.title: Maven/JUnit essentials
tasks.description: Look up standard source/test layout, a dependency, and assertions.
tasks.criteria: explain what the Maven test phase does and where a test belongs.

tasks.title: package the small exercise and test it
tasks.description: Create a minimal Maven exercise when you reach this task; add JUnit Jupiter compatible with your JDK. This is still learner-created work, not an entire backend scaffold.
tasks.criteria: terminal test run passes at least three scenarios: valid creation, changing one object's state independently, and repository lookup. Intentionally break one behavior to see a test fail, then restore it. Save the command/report summary. Carry these classes into the later app instead of restarting from another tutorial.

tasks.title: Python practice
tasks.description: Continue the current certificate unit; if reviewing basics, practice functions, lists/dictionaries, and a simple transformation.
tasks.criteria: one rerunnable notebook/script or a finished provider lab; explain one input/output and one error you corrected.

tasks.title: exceptions and validation
tasks.description: Read only what is needed for blank titles and missing tasks.
tasks.criteria: describe which layer decides validity and what the caller sees when an operation fails.

tasks.title: create a small service
tasks.description: Move create/find/change-status use cases behind a service using constructor-supplied repository dependency.
tasks.criteria: a runner calls the service rather than manipulating storage directly; both valid and missing-ID paths are deliberate. Explain dependency injection here as passing a dependency through the constructor.

tasks.title: negative tests
tasks.description: Add at least one invalid-title test and one missing-ID test; avoid catch-all exception handling.
tasks.criteria: both fail if their behavior is removed and pass normally; total suite has at least four meaningful tests. Record any unfinished rule as a blocker.

tasks.title: current web lab
tasks.description: Verify current HTML/CSS rubric; use lab02's noted TODOs only if still relevant.
tasks.criteria: evidence for one layout check at wide/narrow widths, one form validation case, and asset loading; record remaining rubric items. Do not assume an existing “published” note proves today's behavior or submission.

tasks.title: SQL and HTTP preview
tasks.description: Read a brief explanation of primary/foreign keys and GET vs POST.
tasks.criteria: explain a task identifier, a future course reference, and the different purpose of the two HTTP methods.

tasks.title: relational exercise
tasks.description: Sketch Course → StudyTask and write three proposed queries: list tasks, filter by status, count tasks per course. Execute in an existing suitable SQL environment if available; otherwise mark results as predictions to run in Week 02.
tasks.criteria: diagram, three query attempts, predicted results for a tiny dataset, and a clear “executed” or “not yet executed” label. No database setup rabbit hole today.

tasks.title: certificate lab
tasks.description: Spend up to 30m on required explanation and the rest implementing its lab. If choosing a review exercise, load a tiny CSV with Python, validate rows, and summarize one field.
tasks.criteria: notebook/script reruns and produces one explained result; log incomplete assessments honestly. This does not imply finishing a whole course unit in two hours.

tasks.title: current database lab
tasks.description: Use the assigned tool. If Countries/Cities is still current, independently explain PK/FK, reproduce one filter and one INNER/LEFT JOIN comparison, then check submission requirements.
tasks.criteria: two query results or design-view evidence, explanation of unmatched rows, and actual submission status recorded. Do not replace a required Base artifact with a PostgreSQL exercise.

tasks.title: demo
tasks.description: From the terminal, create/list/find/change a task and run tests.
tasks.criteria: commands and results logged; name one behavior proved by a negative test.

tasks.title: G1 assessment
tasks.description: Without copying, explain a constructor, interface, typed collection, missing/invalid input handling, Maven dependency, and GET vs POST.
tasks.criteria: G1 marked passed only if those explanations and at least four passing meaningful tests exist. Mark precise gaps otherwise.

tasks.title: review and Week 02 setup
tasks.description: Fill the weekly template, check deadlines for the next 14 days, and select next week's three outcomes.
tasks.criteria: revised B/I/A hours, at most two carryovers, and the first action for Day 1 recorded. G1 gaps use the bounded repair path in ROADMAP; unfinished SQL preview can be deferred.

weeks.title: Start Spring Boot and expose a small API

tasks.title: verify G1 and versions
tasks.description: Re-run Week 01 tests, explain the constructor/repository boundary, and check JDK compatibility with your chosen stable Spring Boot version.
tasks.criteria: G1 and chosen versions recorded. If prerequisites fail, use today's full 2h B block for targeted repair instead, then reassess next session; defer SQL preview if needed to start Spring later this week.

tasks.title: generate the smallest app at this point
tasks.description: Use Spring Initializr with Maven and Spring Web; retain its wrapper and compatible test dependencies. Bring over useful Week 01 classes, avoiding duplicate tutorial implementations.
tasks.criteria: wrapper builds/tests from terminal and the application starts locally. Record the actual project path. Database/JPA/Docker dependencies can wait.

tasks.title: first read endpoint
tasks.description: Implement a GET task-list endpoint using a small in-memory dependency, consulting at most 15m of the REST guide.
tasks.criteria: a terminal HTTP request to /api/tasks returns 200 and valid JSON; explain URL → controller → response in your own words. The list may initially be empty.

tasks.title: OS processes/current lab
tasks.description: Follow the actual brief. If no urgent replacement, observe a harmless process, PID/parent relationship, normal termination, and exit status.
tasks.criteria: three command/output observations and an explanation of process vs program; required lab code stays in the assigned language.

tasks.title: Spring bean/constructor injection reading
tasks.description: Compare it with passing the repository to the service in Week 01.
tasks.criteria: explain who constructs the controller/service and why constructor injection helps testing.

tasks.title: POST and service wiring
tasks.description: Add a small create request/response and wire controller → service → repository.
tasks.criteria: POST returns 201, a generated ID, and a Location header; a subsequent GET finds the created task. No persistence is claimed yet.

tasks.title: keep service tests running
tasks.description: Run old tests against the adapted service; add or adjust a creation test when necessary.
tasks.criteria: service behavior remains tested without starting the whole web application; record passing results.

tasks.title: current certificate unit
tasks.description: Continue its Python/data lab.
tasks.criteria: one completed small segment or reproducible intermediate artifact and a next step logged; use a function/list/dictionary exercise if basics still need repair.

tasks.title: HTTP semantics
tasks.description: Review path parameters, JSON, 400, 404, and status updates.
tasks.criteria: write an expected-status table for valid create/read/update, blank title, invalid status, and missing task.

tasks.title: implement the next vertical slice
tasks.description: Add read-by-ID and PATCH status through the service. Handle missing numeric IDs explicitly and reject invalid input using the simplest compatible approach; formal validation refactoring comes in Week 04.
tasks.criteria: create → read → change status → read works; missing ID gives 404, blank title and unknown status give 400 rather than 500.

tasks.title: exercise domain/service boundaries
tasks.description: Add or refine tests for missing-ID and invalid-status handling.
tasks.criteria: at least one test verifies each failure behavior, and unchanged tasks retain their state.

tasks.title: current OOP exercise
tasks.description: Implement or independently recheck the current Java rubric, using inheritance/interfaces only if useful or required.
tasks.criteria: runnable evidence for two required behaviors and one boundary case, plus submission status. Do not rewrite a working lab to imitate Spring patterns.

tasks.title: web-test lookup
tasks.description: Read the testing section matching your selected Spring Boot version.
tasks.criteria: distinguish a service unit test from an HTTP/controller test and choose a compatible approach.

tasks.title: automate HTTP cases
tasks.description: Write tests for create, list/read, status change, missing ID, blank title, and unknown status. Assert meaningful status and response content rather than only application startup.
tasks.criteria: at least five meaningful HTTP tests cover both success and failure, terminal build passes, and a deliberately broken status/validation rule makes a test fail before restoring it. Record any scenario still untested.

tasks.title: data exercise
tasks.description: Continue the current lab, or read a small local CSV and calculate a grouped/count summary if ready.
tasks.criteria: reproducible artifact with one interpretation and one input-quality check. Do not skip unresolved Python prerequisites to reach pandas early.

tasks.title: SQL/JDBC reading
tasks.description: Select keys, joins, and parameterized queries from Amazon's database course or the PostgreSQL tutorial.
tasks.criteria: explain why SQL parameters are different from concatenating user input into a query.

tasks.title: set up a disposable PostgreSQL database and practice
tasks.description: Use local PostgreSQL or a database-only container. Record the version and connection method without secret values. Create a tiny Course/StudyTask sample schema and run select, filter, join, group/count, and insert exercises. This is SQL practice; the API still uses memory.
tasks.criteria: five executed query/command results with predicted-vs-actual notes, including a course with no tasks and an intentional FK violation. Leave JDBC coding to Week 03 rather than build another application. If setup blocks for 30m, record the error, write query attempts, and reserve the first Week 03 block for setup; do not claim execution.

tasks.title: current web task
tasks.description: Follow the rubric; if appropriate, practice one DOM/event or form behavior and inspect its HTTP request.
tasks.criteria: one browser-visible behavior and request/validation evidence recorded. If Flask has already been assigned, replace this with the actual Flask task immediately.

tasks.title: document current behavior
tasks.description: Write app run/test commands and manual request examples, including the memory-only storage limitation and reset behavior.
tasks.criteria: instructions reproduce create → read → update and at least one error. Record actual commands; do not present future PostgreSQL support as complete.

tasks.title: internship baseline
tasks.description: Explain your request flow aloud for five minutes; answer three questions on encapsulation, collections, and HTTP; list two strengths and two gaps.
tasks.criteria: short notes include one design tradeoff and the next practice target. Review your Git diff and make a focused commit if ready.

tasks.title: certificate lab
tasks.description: Continue the currently appropriate lab, spending more time running/editing than watching.
tasks.criteria: rerunnable output, three observations, and actual certificate progress logged. If unfinished, identify the next specific step rather than rushing to the next unit.

tasks.title: current database assignment
tasks.description: Practice in its required tool; choose joins/aggregation if the rubric leaves a gap.
tasks.criteria: two query results and an explanation of the zero-match case; verify any imminent submission separately from portfolio work.

tasks.title: API demo
tasks.description: Start from an empty in-memory store; create a task, read it, change status, show one 400 and one 404, and run tests.
tasks.criteria: exact commands/results and app revision recorded. State that restart loses in-memory tasks.

tasks.title: G2 review
tasks.description: Explain controller/service/repository responsibilities, constructor injection, PK/FK, a join, and parameterized SQL.
tasks.criteria: mark passed only with the HTTP flow and explanations; flag missing PostgreSQL setup/query execution for the first Week 03 block.

tasks.title: replan
tasks.description: Fill the weekly review, check real AGH deadlines, and refine the Week 03 outline.
tasks.criteria: three outcomes, actual hours, at most two essential carryovers, and a first action recorded. If the API is unfinished, simplify optional documentation/interview work before expanding database scope.

tasks.description: current Java collections/OOP exercise.

tasks.title: current database keys/normalization topic

tasks.criteria: checkpoint marked from evidence, upcoming AGH deadlines checked, next three outcomes and revised hours recorded.

weeks.title: Relationships, validation, and a clear error contract
weeks.checkpoint: course/task relation and consistent client errors work in HTTP and PostgreSQL. No advanced many-to-many model or authentication project is needed.

tasks.title: Validate API requests

tasks.criteria: document required versus optional fields; blank title, unknown status, and malformed input each return 400; normal create remains 201.

tasks.title: current IPC topic or lab

tasks.title: Link tasks to courses

tasks.criteria: create a course and linked task, query the relationship, reject a missing course, and demonstrate FK enforcement in PostgreSQL.

tasks.description: current Java exceptions exercise.

tasks.criteria: both attempts include an edge case and an explanation; refactor preserves passing tests.
